question:
6. The following table gives the distribution of the workers in a community by age, sex and type of work.

\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrr}
\text{Age in Years (last birthday)} & \text{Manual Male} & \text{Manual Female} & \text{Non-manual Male} & \text{Non-manual Female}\\
5\text{-}10&8&15&0&0\\
11\text{-}15&10&20&0&0\\
16\text{-}20&22&20&25&5\\
21\text{-}35&35&45&65&25\\
36\text{-}50&25&35&45&15\\
51\text{-}65&20&15&15&5\\
\text{above }65&10&5&0&0
\end{array}
\]

A similar table that was produced for the same community ten years ago is as follows:

\[
\begin{array}{c|rr}
\text{Age in years (last birthday)}&\text{Manual}&\text{Non-manual}\\
5\text{-}10&15&0\\
11\text{-}15&35&0\\
16\text{-}20&40&40\\
21\text{-}35&50&80\\
36\text{-}50&70&65\\
51\text{-}65&20&15\\
\text{above }65&10&0
\end{array}
\]

The break-up of workers by sex is not given in the old table. Assume that the male-female ratios in both the '35 and below' and 'above 35' age-groups have remained the same over the last ten years for manual as well as non-manual workers. In which of these two age-groups has the number of female manual workers increased more?

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
